ai_root_cause: VLAN 30 is not created on MS1, so there is no SVI for VLAN 30 and thus no gateway or DHCP relay for PCs in that VLAN.
evidence: MS1#show vlan brief -> VLAN Name Status 1 default active 10 users active 20 finance active 40 wireless active (VLAN 30 absent)
fix_steps: MS1(config)# vlan 30 | MS1(config-vlan)# name users30 | MS1(config-vlan)# exit | MS1(config)# interface vlan30 | MS1(config-if)# ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0 | MS1(config-if)# no shutdown

ai_root_cause: MS1 VLAN10 SVI lacks an ip helper-address, so DHCP requests from PC1 are not forwarded to SRV_DHCP.
evidence: MS1#show run interface Vlan10 -> interface Vlan10 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0 no ip helper-address
fix_steps: MS1(config)# interface Vlan10 | MS1(config-if)# ip helper-address 192.168.30.5

ai_root_cause: Access port SW2 Gi0/1 is configured in VLAN 20 instead of the data VLAN (likely VLAN 30), placing PC3 in the wrong subnet.
evidence: SW2#show interfaces Gi0/1 switchport -> Access Mode VLAN: 20 (finance)
fix_steps: SW2(config)# interface Gi0/1 | SW2(config-if)# switchport access vlan 30

ai_root_cause: SRV_DNS DNS service is disabled, preventing hostname resolution while IP-based ping works.
evidence: SRV_DNS: Services > DNS DNS Service: OFF A records: 3 loaded
fix_steps: SRV_DNS# services dns start

ai_root_cause: MS1 lacks a default route (gateway of last resort) to forward traffic to the edge router R1, so internal VLANs have no path to the Internet.
evidence: Gateway last resort is not set

ai_root_cause: Interface Gi0/2 on SW1 is administratively shut down.
evidence: SW1#show ip interface brief -> Gi0/2 unassigned YES manual administratively down down
fix_steps: SW1(config)# interface Gi0/2 | SW1(config-if)# no shutdown

ai_root_cause: Trunk port on SW1 Gi0/1 does not allow VLAN 30, so DHCP requests from VLAN 30 hosts never reach MS1.
evidence: SW1#show interfaces trunk -> Gi0/1 Allowed VLANs: 10,20,40
fix_steps: SW1(config)# interface Gi0/1 | SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30

ai_root_cause: Both PCs have been assigned the same IP address 192.168.10.11, likely due to a DHCP server handing out duplicate addresses or a static IP misconfiguration.
evidence: PC1> ipconfig IPv4 Address: 192.168.10.11 | PC2> ipconfig IPv4 Address: 192.168.10.11
fix_steps: Determine MAC addresses of PC1 and PC2 (ipconfig /all). | On the DHCP server (SRV_DHCP), exclude 192.168.10.11 from the address pool or create a reservation for one of the PCs based on its MAC address. | Have the affected PC release and renew its IP address (ipconfig /release && ipconfig /renew). | Verify that each PC now has a unique IP address in VLAN 10.

ai_root_cause: PC9 has an incorrect default gateway set to 192.168.20.1 instead of the correct VLAN10 gateway 192.168.10.1, preventing off-subnet communication.
evidence: PC9> ipconfig -> Default Gateway: 192.168.20.1
fix_steps: PC9> ipconfig set gateway 192.168.10.1 | PC9> ipconfig (verify)

ai_root_cause: ACL 101 is incorrectly applied inbound on Gi0/0 instead of Serial0/0/0, blocking branch traffic to SRV_DNS.
evidence: R2#show ip interface Gi0/0 -> Inbound access list is 101 | R2#show ip interface Serial0/0/0 -> Inbound access list is not set
fix_steps: R2(config)# interface Serial0/0/0 | R2(config-if)# ip access-group 101 in | R2(config-if)# exit | R2(config)# interface Gi0/0 | R2(config-if)# no ip access-group 101 in

ai_root_cause: R2 is not learning OSPF routes for the HQ subnets (192.168.10.0/24, 192.168.20.0/24, 192.168.30.0/24, 192.168.40.0/24), indicating OSPF adjacency or route advertisement is missing.
evidence: Gateway last resort is 10.10.10.1 network 0.0.0.0 | C 10.10.10.0/30 directly connected, Serial0/0/0 | S* 0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 10.10.10.1
fix_steps: If OSPF neighbor with R1 is not up: |   R2(config)# interface Serial0/0/0 |   R2(config-if)# ip ospf 1 area 0 | If neighbor is up but routes are still missing, verify R1 OSPF network statements for the HQ subnets and ensure they are advertised.

ai_root_cause: IP address conflict: PC5 is configured with static IP 192.168.30.55, which is also leased by the DHCP server (SRV_DHCP) to PC6, causing PC5 to lose its IP connectivity.
evidence: PC5> ipconfig ... IPv4 Address: 192.168.30.55 (static) | SRV_DHCP bindings: 192.168.30.55 leased to PC6
fix_steps: SRV_DHCP# configure terminal | SRV_DHCP(config)# ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.30.55 | SRV_DHCP(config)# exit | SRV_DHCP# write memory

ai_root_cause: NAT ACL 1 on R1 lacks a permit entry for the 192.168.40.0/24 subnet, so traffic from VLAN 40 wireless users is not translated for Internet access.

10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255
20 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255
30 permit 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255
fix_steps: R1(config)# access-list 1 permit 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255

ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool on SRV_DHCP is handing out an incorrect DNS server address (192.168.30.11) instead of the correct DNS server at 192.168.30.10, causing DNS resolution to fail for all clients.
evidence: SRV_DHCP pool VLAN10 default-router 192.168.10.1 dns-server 192.168.30.11
fix_steps: SRV_DHCP(config)# ip dhcp pool VLAN10 | SRV_DHCP(dhcp-config)# dns-server 192.168.30.10

ai_root_cause: SW1 is incorrectly elected as the root bridge for VLAN 10 due to having a lower spanning-tree priority than MS1, causing suboptimal uplink paths.
evidence: SW1#show spanning-tree vlan 10 -> Root ID Priority 8192 This bridge is root
fix_steps: SW1(config)# spanning-tree vlan 10 priority 36864

ai_root_cause: The laptop wireless profile SSID (netsage-staff) does not match the AP's SSID (NetSage-Staff) causing association failures.
evidence: AP1 status: SSID NetSage-Staff, WPA2-PSK enabled | Laptop profile: SSID netsage-staff (mismatch)
fix_steps: On the affected laptop, open wireless network settings. | Edit the wireless profile for the staff network. | Change the SSID to exactly NetSage-Staff (matching case). | Retain the existing WPA2-PSK passphrase. | Save the profile and attempt reconnection.

ai_root_cause: Physical link failure on MS1 Gi0/3 (cable disconnected/misconnected) causing the interface to be down/down and breaking connectivity to R1 and the rest of the site.
evidence: MS1#show ip interface brief -> Gi0/3 192.168.254.2 YES manual down down
fix_steps: Physically reconnect the cable between MS1 Gi0/3 and R1 Gi0/0 | MS1(config)# interface Gi0/3 | MS1(config-if)# no shutdown

ai_root_cause: SW2 interface Gi0/2 is in err-disabled state due to a port-security violation (psecure-violation).
evidence: Gi0/2 err-disabled psecure-violation
fix_steps: SW2# configure terminal | SW2(config)# interface Gi0/2 | SW2(config-if)# shutdown | SW2(config-if)# no shutdown

ai_root_cause: The VLAN 20 SVI on MS1 is configured with an incorrect subnet mask (255.255.252.0 instead of 255.255.255.0), causing hosts in VLAN 20 to have mismatched IP addressing and weird reachability.
evidence: MS1#show run interface Vlan20 -> ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.252.0 | MS1#show run interface Vlan20 -> interface Vlan20 ext-side ip address 192.168.20.5 255.255.255.0
fix_steps: MS1# configure terminal | MS1(config)# interface Vlan20 | MS1(config-if)# no ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.252.0 | MS1(config-if)# ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0 | MS1(config-if)# no ip address 192.168.20.5 255.255.255.0 | MS1(config-if)# end | MS1# write memory

ai_root_cause: OSPF area mismatch on the Serial0/0/0 link: R1 is configured for area 0 while R2 is configured for area 1, preventing adjacency formation.
evidence: R1#show run | sec ospf -> network 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.3 area 0 | Topology note indicates R2 side configured area 1 | R1#show ip ospf neighbor shows empty neighbor table
fix_steps: R2(config)# interface Serial0/0/0 | R2(config-if)# ip ospf 1 area 0

ai_root_cause: PC10's default gateway is incorrectly set to 192.168.30.10 (the DNS server) instead of the VLAN30 SVI address 192.168.30.1 on MS1, preventing off‑subnet traffic.
evidence:
PC10> ipconfig
Default Gateway: 192.168.30.10
fix_steps: On PC10, open the IP configuration settings and change the Default Gateway to 192.168.30.1

ai_root_cause: R1 VTY lines are configured for Telnet only and no enable secret/enable password is set, making management access insecure.
evidence: line vty 0 4 transport input telnet login | no enable secret or enable password configured (output of 'show run | inc enable' shows none)
fix_steps: R1(config)# enable secret <strong_password> | R1(config)# crypto key generate rsa modulus 1024 | R1(config)# line vty 0 4 | R1(config-line)# transport input ssh | R1(config-line)# login local

ai_root_cause: NAT inside and outside interfaces are reversed on R1 (Gi0/0 marked as outside, Gi0/1 as inside), preventing translation of internal host traffic.
evidence: Outside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/0 | Inside interfaces: GigabitEthernet0/1
fix_steps: R1# configure terminal | R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0 | R1(config-if)# ip nat inside | R1(config-if)# exit | R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | R1(config-if)# ip nat outside | R1(config-if)# end | R1# write memory

ai_root_cause: ACL 101 applied inbound on R1 Gi0/0 denies UDP DNS traffic (port 53) to the internal DNS server at 192.168.30.10.
evidence: Extended IP access list 101 10 deny udp any host 192.168.30.10 eq 53
fix_steps: R1(config)# access-list 101 | R1(config-ext-nacl)# no 10 | R1(config-ext-nacl)# exit | R1(config)# exit

evidence: SRV_DHCP pool VLAN10 utilization: 100% (254 254 leases issued) queued requests: 6
fix_steps: configure terminal | ip dhcp pool VLAN10 | network 192.168.10.0 255.255.254.0 | default-router 192.168.10.1 | dns-server 192.168.30.10 | exit | exit

ai_root_cause: SW2 Gi0/1 is configured as an access port instead of a trunk, preventing a trunk link to MS1.
evidence: SW2#show interfaces Gi0/1 switchport -> Administrative Mode: static access Operational Mode: static access
fix_steps: SW2(config)# interface Gi0/1 | SW2(config-if)# switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q | SW2(config-if)# switchport mode trunk | SW2(config-if)# switchport nonegotiate

ai_root_cause: R2 has an incorrect static route for 192.168.0.0/16 pointing to next-hop 10.10.10.5 instead of the correct next-hop 10.10.10.1 (R1).
The DNS A record for intranet.netsage.local on SRV_DNS points to 192.168.30.99 instead of the correct 192.168.30.10.
evidence: SRV_DNS zone netsage.local intranet A 192.168.30.99
fix_steps: On SRV_DNS, open the DNS zone netsage.local | Locate the A record for intranet | Change the IP address from 192.168.30.99 to 192.168.30.10 | Save the zone and reload if required

evidence: R1#show run | inc nat -> ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | R1#show ip nat translations -> (only one translation active)
fix_steps: R1(config)# no ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | R1(config)# ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload

ai_root_cause: R2 Serial0/0/0 is configured with IP address 10.10.11.2/30 instead of the required 10.10.10.0/30 subnet, causing a Layer 3 mismatch with R1.
evidence: R2#show run interface Serial0/0/0 ip address 10.10.11.2 255.255.255.252 | R2#show ip interface brief Serial0/0/0 10.10.11.2 YES manual up down
fix_steps: R2# configure terminal | R2(config)# interface Serial0/0/0 | R2(config-if)# ip address 10.10.10.2 255.255.255.252 | R2(config-if)# no shutdown | R2(config-if)# end | R2# show ip interface brief Serial0/0/0

ai_root_cause: Portfast is enabled on the uplink port Fa0/1 connecting SW1 to SW2, causing the port to bypass STP listening/learning states and creating temporary loops that trigger frequent TCNs and broadcast storms.
evidence: SW1#show run interface Fa0/1 spanning-tree portfast | SW1#show spanning-tree detail TCN counter incrementing every few minutes
fix_steps: SW1(config)# interface Fa0/1 | SW1(config-if)# no spanning-tree portfast

ai_root_cause: The laptops that fail authentication are using an incorrect WPA2-PSK passphrase, causing repeated 4-way handshake failures.
evidence: AP1 association log: WPA2-PSK: multiple 4-way handshake failures from 3 clients
fix_steps: On each affected laptop, open the wireless network properties for the SSID | Set the security type to WPA2-Personal (WPA2-PSK) | Enter the passphrase netsage123 | Reconnect to the wireless network and verify successful authentication

ai_root_cause: ACL 102 on R1 has a permissive 'permit ip any any' ACE (sequence 10) placed before the 'deny tcp any any eq 80' ACE (sequence 20), so HTTP traffic is always permitted and the block never triggers.
evidence: 10 permit ip any any | 20 deny tcp any any eq 80
fix_steps: R1(config)# no access-list 102 | R1(config)# ip access-list extended 102 | R1(config-ext-nacl)# deny tcp any any eq 80 | R1(config-ext-nacl)# permit ip any any | R1(config-ext-nacl)# exit | R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0 | R1(config-if)# ip access-group 102 in | R1(config-if)# end
